whyThisShow: This is a May '77 show with a legitimate claim on the whole month, not just a footnote to Cornell. One reviewer argues that "it is entirely possible to suggest that 5-22 is the better all-around show and should therefore be in the 'Best Ever' discussion" [source: 'it is entirely possible to suggest that 5-22 is the better all-around show and should therefore be in the "Best Ever" discussion']. The Help>Slip>Franklin's that opens the second set draws particular attention, with one listener calling it "easily a top-3 of all-time" [source: 'Help on the Way -> Slipknot! -> Franklin\'s Tower is easily a top-3 of all-time, and one could argue this is the best sequence ever performed!']. The back half of the second set — Estimated Prophet into The Other One into Wharf Rat into Terrapin into Morning Dew — is substantial: one reviewer describes this Dew as "quite remarkable, with a long, spiraling jam that starts out very quite and mellow and progresses into a full-out assault on the auditory senses" [source: 'This Dew is also quite remarkable, with a long, spiraling jam that starts out very quite and mellow and progresses into a full-out assault on the auditory senses']. The one practical caveat: Dick's Picks Vol. 3 drew only eight songs from this night, and one reviewer notes "One of the reasons I don't play DP3 very much is because it is not the complete show" [source: 'One of the reasons I don\'t play DP3 very much is because it is not the complete show'] — the Archive identifier has the rest.
listenFor: Start with the Help>Slip>Franklin's — one listener places it among the best sequences the band ever played [source: 'Help on the Way -> Slipknot! -> Franklin\'s Tower is easily a top-3 of all-time, and one could argue this is the best sequence ever performed!']. Then track the Sugaree in the first set: one reviewer calls it "nothing less than brilliant," ranking it second only to the Fox Theater version played two shows earlier [source: 'The Sugaree is nothing less than brilliant; of all the versions of this special song, this one ranks second only to the slightly more blissful and longer version played two shows previously at the Fox Theater in Atlanta']. Another listener goes further, calling it "the best ever done" [source: 'I have so many favorites in this show (Sugaree included...and yes, it is the best ever done)']. Stay through the segue late in the second set, where one reviewer specifically flags "the segue from an abbreviated Terrapin right into Morning Dew" as worth your attention [source: 'Check out the segue from an abbreviated Terrapin right into Morning Dew']. The soundboard recording rewards close listening: one reviewer describes "well balanced vocals and instruments with just the slightest touch of reverb" [source: 'Well balanced vocals and instruments with just the slightest touch of reverb'].
context: This is a May 1977 show at the Sportatorium in Pembroke Pines, Florida, from one of the most celebrated touring runs in the band's history. The best available recording is a soundboard (identifier: gd77-05-22.sbd.dp-leftovers.18803.sbefail.shnf), and the Archive identifier specifically contains the songs left off the official release. Dick's Picks Vol. 3 was the first official 1977 release from Dick Latvala's series, but it drew only a partial selection from this night; the Archive recording fills in what the official release omitted, including Peggy-O, Friend of the Devil, Ramble on Rose, and Brown-Eyed Women [source: 'Look at all these Jerry songs that didn\'t make the cut...Peggy-O, Freind of the Devil, Ramble On Rose, Brown-Eyed Women...WTF?']. To hear the full show in sequence, listeners assemble the DP3 tracks alongside this Archive source.
funFact: One reviewer reports that before a now-defunct trading site went dark, they managed to download every song not on Dick's Picks and burn the complete 24-song concert to CD, calling the quality and clarity "second-to-none" [source: 'I have all 24 songs from this incredible mind-blowing concert!!!!! And the quality and clarity of these songs is second-to-none'].
headline: Pembroke Pines, May '77 — the show Dick only half released.
